the_one_metric: Timing/confirmation of the second Phase 3 VDPHL01 male readout in H2 2026 and cash runway to NDA - not any P&L line, since the company is pre-revenue
whats_priced_in: A $4.3bn clinical-stage valuation already reflects April Phase 3 male data and the positive 15 July Phase 2 female topline, so the print is a spend-and-timing update rather than a catalyst.
bear_case: With 86.7% realised vol and only two prior prints (both negative, -3.91% and -7.14%), a cautious runway comment or a slipped second Phase 3 date could easily cut double digits off a name 199% above its 52w low.
key_drivers: Pre-revenue biotech: earnings is a low-information event; the real catalyst (Phase 2 female data) already cleared on 15 July 2026
Base rate is unusable - only two prior earnings events since the Feb 2026 IPO, both modestly negative
Realised vol 86.7% annualised (~5.5% daily) means a large move is likely irrespective of content
Run-up +8.7% over 5d into the print against a flat 20d (+0.52%); Baron Health Care Fund a disclosed holder and constructive
Coverage gap: one keepable news document in a 14-day window, no sell-side preview in the corpus
what_would_change_my_mind: An 8-K or release language pulling forward or deferring the second Phase 3 male readout would turn this from a non-event into a directional one.
reasoning: Pre-revenue names do not trade on the Q2 print; they trade on the next readout. Both prior prints fell, but n=2 is no base rate. Enormous ambient vol dominates: I have far more confidence in size (~7%) than in sign. Neutral, honestly held.

the_one_metric: Pipeline timing and cash runway commentary; the print has no revenue line the market underwrites
whats_priced_in: A 16.2% 20-day run-up into a close 2.7% off the 52-week high says the good pipeline news is already in the tape.
bear_case: Immunome's earnings prints are historically damp (median 3.02%, none beyond 7%) so a modest fade is as likely as a real drawdown, and any brought-forward readout reprices it up hard.
key_drivers: Stock 2.7% off 52w high, +192% off the low, +16.2% over 20 sessions - fully told story into the event
Prior eight reactions skew negative: 5 down, mean -0.14%, median absolute 3.02%
Corpus shows a -9.9% pre-market day on 5 Aug after a +9% session: the regime is jumpy well above the 42.5% 20d realised vol
Heavy Form 4 cadence Jun-Aug and a 12 Jun 8-K that is only Item 5.07 annual-meeting results - no material corporate signal
Coverage gap: one keepable news document, and it is a pre-market movers list, not a preview
what_would_change_my_mind: A dated near-term clinical readout or partnership disclosed with the release would override the sell-the-run-up read.
reasoning: Clinical-stage biotech at 52-week highs after a 16% run, reporting a quarter with nothing to beat. Historical reactions are small and negatively skewed. That is a modest fade setup, not a thesis. Size dominated by the elevated single-name vol regime evidenced in the corpus.

the_one_metric: Pro-forma cash and opex ramp after the $200m Tanabe royalty buyout and $100m Tranche A draw, against the 22 Dec 2026 PDUFA date
whats_priced_in: The stock is a December PDUFA option 42% below its 52-week high; the Q2 print is a bookkeeping update on a launch build that is already known.
bear_case: The June financing package - $200m cash out to Tanabe, secured debt with a minimum-liquidity covenant, plus a 424B5 - makes the cash line the one thing that can genuinely surprise, and a thin runway disclosure would hit hard.
key_drivers: NDA accepted with a PDUFA target of 22 Dec 2026: the binary sits well after this print and dominates the equity
June 2026 restructuring of capital - Tanabe royalty buyout for $200m, $500m BioPharma Credit facility with $100m drawn, concurrent 424B5 - all already disclosed
Realised vol only 23.9% annualised and 20d run-up +0.18%: the market is not positioning for this event
Last two prints were small and negative (-2.56%, -2.96%); the 8-event median is 4.42% but the tail comes from 2024
Coverage gap: zero news documents captured for this event - filings-only read
what_would_change_my_mind: Any statement on pre-approval inspection status, launch timing, or a revised PDUFA expectation would make this a directional print.
reasoning: Everything material was disclosed in March and June. What is left is a quiet cash-and-opex quarter in front of a December decision, in a name whose realised vol has collapsed to 24%. Genuinely split, and the news blackout in the corpus lowers evidence quality further. Neutral by evidence, not by hedge.

the_one_metric: Fiscal Q4 revenue and EPS guidance, and within it the leading-edge/HBM versus China mature-node mix commentary that decides whether the WFE cycle narrative holds
whats_priced_in: Up 109.8% year to date but 26.1% below the 52-week high and -4.7% over 20 sessions, so the AI-capex bull case is owned while the recent correction has already taken some risk out.
bear_case: The corpus itself carries the AI-capex-durability bear argument, and a name that has doubled in a year with 84% realised vol can gap far lower on a single soft guide regardless of the beat.
key_drivers: FY26 consensus EPS $12.14, revised up 3 cents in the prior seven days - modest positive revision drift into the print
Stock de-risked into the event: -26.1% from the 52-week high, -4.7% over 20 days, +1.34% over 5 days
Sharp conflict between the anchors' base rate (8 prints, median 1.36%, none beyond 2.29%) and 84.4% realised 20d vol implying ~5.3% daily - I weight the vol regime for sizing
Peer read-through is supportive: SMCI guided FY27 sales to $65-72bn from $39.1bn on record AI backlog
Macro fragility is a live corpus theme - VIX 15.28, Burry publicly short semis and questioning AI capex durability
what_would_change_my_mind: A China revenue-share or export-control disclosure in the Q4 guide would flip the direction regardless of the headline beat.
reasoning: Estimates drifting up while the stock sits a quarter below its high is the mildest of positive setups. I hold direction lightly. The load-bearing judgement is size: an eight-print base rate under 1.4% cannot survive an 84% realised vol regime, so I size to the tape, not the history.

the_one_metric: Organic revenue growth against the 5.2% consensus, and whether the 38% year-to-date backlog build is actually converting into sales
whats_priced_in: At 0.46% below the 52-week high, $310 against a $316.86 average target, 32.1x earnings versus a 27.4x industry, the stock is priced for clean conversion of the backlog.
bear_case: Backlog up 18% year over year and 38% year to date is a genuine forward asset, five of the last eight prints rose, and a raised full-year EPS guide would carry the stock through a soft top line as it did last quarter.
key_drivers: Consensus revenue growth 5.2% y/y, decelerating from 12.1% in the year-ago quarter; estimates merely reconfirmed over 30 days - no upgrade momentum
Documented pattern of missing revenue estimates repeatedly over two years, including a significant organic revenue miss last quarter
Only 2.3% headroom to the average analyst price target with the stock at its 52-week high after +8.6% in a month
Valuation stretched on both corpus measures: 32.1x P/E vs 27.4x industry, and a 15.1% premium to a $264 DCF
Peer read-through is mixed and unkind: Kennametal beat on revenue and still traded down 6.1%
what_would_change_my_mind: An organic growth print comfortably above 5% with a raised full-year revenue guide would justify the multiple and reverse the call.
reasoning: A fully valued compounder at its high, at its price target, with no estimate momentum and a habit of top-line misses. The asymmetry is against it. But the setup is legible, which means it is at least partly priced, so I keep the score small. Low vol (18.5%) caps the size.

the_one_metric: Comparable store sales, and whether the reaffirmed 1-2% full-year comp guide and 3.80-4.50% adjusted operating margin guide finally get raised
whats_priced_in: Up 44.2% in 2026 with options pricing a 12.74% swing, the market expects a turnaround beat and is arguing only about how big.
bear_case: Sign has been a coin flip across eight prints (four up, four down, including -17.83% and -8.02%), and management reaffirming rather than raising after a 3.5% Q1 comp may itself be the tell that the second half is harder.
key_drivers: Real option-implied move of 12.74% in the corpus - the only event here with one; calibration says most names do not break the implied
Consensus $2.04bn revenue and $0.80 EPS; the bar is comps, turnaround progress and margin recovery
Q1'26 comps +3.5%, strongest in five years, adjusted operating margin +410bp to 3.8% - yet full-year comp guide left at 1-2%, a conservative bar with room to raise
History is violent and two-sided: +57.04%, +14.40%, -17.83%, -8.04%, -8.02%; median absolute 8.03%
Coverage gap: a single keepable news document, and it is an implied-move screen rather than a fundamental preview
what_would_change_my_mind: A comp print below 1% or any walk-back of the 3.80-4.50% adjusted operating margin guide turns this decisively down.
reasoning: The direction here is honestly a coin flip: four up, four down, and a conservative guide that could be raised or defended. What I can say with real evidence is the size. Options price 12.74%; the eight-print median is 8.03%; realised typically undershoots implied. I size at 8.5% and refuse a direction.

the_one_metric: Billings and the FY27 revenue guide - specifically whether the outlook is raised a second consecutive quarter, since revenue itself is near-certain to clear $319m
whats_priced_in: At $33.32 against a $33.25 average target, 1.9% off the 52-week high and up 10.5% in a month, a beat-and-raise is the consensus expectation rather than a surprise.
bear_case: Box has a documented history of exceeding expectations, raised the FY27 outlook only last quarter, and productivity-software sentiment is strong with the peer group up 16.4% in a month - a clean billings beat could still take it through the highs.
key_drivers: Zero headroom to consensus: share price $33.32 versus a $33.25 average analyst target, at the 52-week high
Consensus $0.40 EPS on $319.09m revenue (+8.6% y/y), merely in line with the 8.9% of a year ago - decelerating, not accelerating
Estimates only reconfirmed over 30 days; no upward revision momentum to underwrite a re-rating
The last two prints both fell (-3.71%, -2.40%) despite the beat history - beats have stopped paying
Analyst dispersion is wide and stale: targets from $26 Underperform to $45 Buy, several unchanged since Aug 2025
what_would_change_my_mind: A meaningful billings or RPO acceleration attributed to AI seat monetisation, paired with a second FY27 raise, would break the sell-the-beat pattern.
reasoning: The last two quarters Box beat and the stock fell. It now enters the print at its 52-week high, exactly at the average target, after a 10.5% month, with a modest 8.6% growth bar and no estimate momentum. That is where beats stop paying. Small score - the pattern is visible to everyone.

the_one_metric: Initial fiscal 2027 sales and EPS guidance - this is the fiscal Q4 print, and the guide, not the quarter, sets the reaction
whats_priced_in: A 15.7% discount to the 52-week high and a flat-to-down 20 days say expectations are already modest, but Baird's fresh $95 to $105 target raise shows the sell side is looking for a constructive FY27 frame.
bear_case: The stock is already de-rated, Mobile Solutions (+8.1%) and Life Sciences (+12.7%) are compounding nicely, the dividend has risen 30 straight years, and management has a habit of guiding conservatively then beating - a low first FY27 bar could be taken well.
key_drivers: Fiscal Q4 print carries the first FY27 guide: the highest-variance disclosure of Donaldson's year
Documented margin pressure: cost of sales up 5.8% and up 100bp as a share of revenue to 66% over nine months
Industrial Solutions contracting (-0.6% in fiscal Q3) with aerospace and defence soft on supply chain
Reaction history is large relative to a 20.4% realised vol: -11.73%, +7.49%, -6.90%, median absolute 6.90% on only five captured events
Positioning modest - 20d run-up -2.2%, 5d -0.76%, Zacks Rank #3 Hold, versus a fresh Baird PT raise to $105
what_would_change_my_mind: An initial FY27 guide with sales growth at or above the FY26 3-5% pace and flat-to-better gross margin would flip this positive.
reasoning: Fiscal-year-opening guides from industrials with rising cost of sales and one shrinking segment skew conservative, and DCI's worst prints (-11.73%, -6.90%) came on guide disappointments. Offsetting that, the stock is already 15.7% off its high with no run-up. Small negative tilt; the sizeable expected move reflects a five-event history far wider than the 20% vol implies.
